column1: # Tests claimed to be deletable, and what each claim was put to.
# A test marked for deletion because a reader found a sentence persuasive is
# a test deleted on agreement. Two passes read all 933 test files and each
# wrote such a sentence; where they agreed, they agreed with each other, not
# with a measurement. So each claim is recorded here with a verdict, and the
# verdict comes from tests/prove_delete.py, which measures it:
#   dead       the thing the test names is in no source file, and running
#              the test produces no passing assertion about behaviour
#   redundant  every line of the product the candidate runs is also run by
#              the keeper, and every assertion it makes is also asked by the
#              keeper (normalised through the syntax tree)
# Nothing here is deleted while its verdict is `unproved`, and
# tests/test_a_delete_is_proved_not_agreed.py holds that: it re-measures the
# cheap half of every claim on each run (the absent name, the assertions)
# and fails if a candidate has gone without being proved, or a proved
# candidate's keeper has gone with it.
# For a `dead` claim the keeper column names the absent thing, not a file.
#   uv run --no-sync python tests/prove_delete.py           # show verdicts
#   uv run --no-sync python tests/prove_delete.py --write   # record them
